actions.name: activity_report
actions.title: 记录有来源的发现
actions.description: Record a discovery with a source and arbitrary facts in activity. Does not wake the Agent. Source is supplied evidence; origin records the actual caller.

actions.name: agent_wake
actions.title: 唤醒 Agent 的主会话或指定会话
actions.description: Queue a new Agent turn with instruction and trigger facts. The host-configured agent device receives wakes from headless hooks and schedules; no conversation runs on the transfer device. Defaults to that Agent host’s main thread; optional threadId targets a conversation there. Busy turns are never interrupted. Uses the durable followup dispatcher.

actions.name: app_capabilities
actions.title: Read host capability facts
actions.description: Live host facts: app.instance identifies the process; app.capabilities reports supported features, provider/source readiness, credential references and required host setup, settings keys, action effects and remote policy. supported means an implementation exists; available means its declared host prerequisites are met, not a successful network probe. No secrets are accepted or returned. Remote writes follow local semantics; disk deletion/overwrite keep their existing NeedsDecision contract. On headless hosts indexing and download destinations treat media roots as read-only; file-channel operations use actual process permissions. Classic history/player/UI are absent. download.import indexes verified files without inferring identity; roots.remove unregisters the root without deleting indexed facts or disk files. settings exposes only returned keys.

actions.name: app_instance
actions.title: Identify the connected NipaPlay process
actions.description: Live process and main-window facts for this endpoint. Also returned as instance by nipa status. Paths identify this running build; appBundlePath is null on platforms without application bundles. experimentalProfile identifies the isolated lab configuration, not the Next switch.

actions.name: danmaku_align
actions.title: danmaku.align
actions.description: Retired compatibility lookup for existing alignment requestId tasks. New requests return unavailable with migration to danmaku.analyze_alignment and danmaku.update.

actions.name: danmaku_align_apply
actions.title: danmaku.align_apply
actions.description: Legacy recovery only: execute an existing persisted alignment decision option with a task revision check. New analysis returns data and offsets are set through danmaku.update.

actions.name: danmaku_align_keep
actions.title: danmaku.align_keep
actions.description: Legacy recovery only: execute an existing persisted alignment decision option with a task revision check. New analysis returns data and offsets are set through danmaku.update.

actions.name: danmaku_analyze_alignment
actions.title: danmaku.analyze_alignment
actions.description: Estimate a fixed offset from up to 100 supplied source/media time anchors. Returns the upper median, absolute residuals in input order, span, evidence and confidence limits. Reads the binding revision; no task, Decision or persistence. Positive integer milliseconds advance danmaku (display time = source time - offsetMs).

actions.name: danmaku_attach
actions.title: danmaku.attach
actions.description: Bind a platform video to entityId, path or the current file (default). Existing platform/video tracks are reused; Classic dandanplay reuse records a binding, with jobId=null. Local pools prevent online acquisition. refresh=true fetches and replaces. Invalid required local ranges fail without mounting; outside-range errors are reported separately. Credentials are opaque host references.

actions.name: danmaku_attach_batch
actions.title: danmaku.attach batch
actions.description: Independent entries in input order using danmaku.attach. All schemas are validated before execution. atomic=false; each index returns its complete outcome (including binding/job IDs, decisions or failure). Successful entries are retained when another fails. Each requestId is scoped exactly as in the single action; credentials remain host references.

actions.name: danmaku_cache_delete
actions.title: danmaku.cache_delete
actions.description: Delete a specific source cache object and unload bindings using it. Binding evidence remains.

actions.name: danmaku_cache_prune
actions.title: danmaku.cache_prune
actions.description: Reclaim oldest recoverable danmaku pools to maxBytes (default 128 MiB). Imported unique copies are excluded. Defers while acquisition tasks are active; unloads evicted pools. Also collects unreferenced content files.

actions.name: danmaku_detach
actions.title: danmaku.detach
actions.description: Revoke this managed binding; unreferenced imported content files are deleted, provenance remains. Recoverable source cache remains subject to the cache budget. Classic local, automatic and Dandanplay tracks remain loaded with their managed binding detached. Other managed tracks are removed.

actions.name: danmaku_episodes
actions.title: danmaku.episodes
actions.description: Read a finite catalogue page. Zero duration means unknown duration. Acquisition requires a finite range within a known media duration.

actions.name: danmaku_export
actions.title: danmaku.export
actions.description: Export one committed binding as JSON to a new file in an authorized media folder. raw preserves original source fields; mapped applies its fixed offset without player filters. Readback is verified.

actions.name: danmaku_fetch
actions.title: danmaku.fetch
actions.description: Create a cancellable segmented acquisition/cache task for one explicit video/range. Does not modify player tracks. requestId makes retries idempotent. A failed acquisition receipt also reports available Classic cache, assigned/partial Next cache and currently loaded matching player tracks; existing comments do not prove this request succeeded.

actions.name: danmaku_fetch_batch
actions.title: danmaku.fetch batch
actions.description: Independent entries in input order using danmaku.fetch. All schemas are validated before execution. atomic=false; each index returns its complete outcome (including binding/job IDs, decisions or failure). Successful entries are retained when another fails. Each requestId is scoped exactly as in the single action; credentials remain host references.

actions.name: danmaku_import
actions.title: danmaku.import
actions.description: Import acquired danmaku using Classic local XML/JSON parsing and encoding support, including ARGB colors. Also accepts normalized JSON arrays (or {comments:[...]}): sourceTimeMs (nonnegative integer milliseconds), text, mode (positive integer), colorRgb (nonnegative integer, converted to RGB); optional platformId, sourceEntryId, originSource, sender, sentAt (strings), fontSize (positive integer). No registered source is required. Supply platform/platformVideoId; host records actor, origin and timestamp. Target entityId (file or episode), path, or current playback (default). Reimport replaces the same platform/video pool atomically, preserving track settings; empty or malformed files are rejected and leave the old track unchanged. Mounted immediately when the target is playing. File data stays in host storage; do not send large comment arrays through tool arguments.

actions.name: danmaku_import_batch
actions.title: danmaku.import batch
actions.description: Independent entries in input order using danmaku.import. All schemas are validated before execution. atomic=false; each index returns its complete outcome (including binding/job IDs, decisions or failure). Successful entries are retained when another fails. Each requestId is scoped exactly as in the single action; credentials remain host references.

actions.name: danmaku_offset
actions.title: danmaku.offset
actions.description: Compatibility alias for danmaku.update: set an absolute fixed offset in integer milliseconds, positive advances, zero resets. Does not refetch or accumulate offsets.

actions.name: danmaku_resolve
actions.title: danmaku.resolve
actions.description: Resolve a public URL or platform ID. Multiple parts return executable selection decisions. No persistence.

actions.name: danmaku_search
actions.title: danmaku.search
actions.description: Bounded transient title search. Unsupported sources report unavailable; no binding or task is created.

actions.name: danmaku_set_dedup
actions.title: danmaku.set_dedup
actions.description: Compatibility alias for danmaku.update: set absolute deduplicate with a binding revision check. deduplicate controls displayFold only; original source cache is preserved.

actions.name: danmaku_set_enabled
actions.title: danmaku.set_enabled
actions.description: Compatibility alias for danmaku.update: set absolute enabled with a binding revision check. deduplicate controls displayFold only; original source cache is preserved.

actions.name: danmaku_sources
actions.title: danmaku.sources
actions.description: List registered sources and capabilities. No network or persistence.

actions.name: danmaku_tracks
actions.title: danmaku.tracks
actions.description: List bindings and all current player tracks, including Classic and local pools with origin/platform/platformVideoId. loaded means mounted in the player registry, including Erika native danmaku; enabled is a track display switch. Neither reports whether comments are currently visible on screen. Accept entityId, path or current (default). Missing file locations are indexed without inferring work identity; no fetch or binding is created.

enabled.description: Track display switch; not proof of visible comments.

loaded.description: Mounted in the player track registry, including Erika native danmaku. Does not prove comments are visible at the current position.

actions.name: danmaku_update
actions.title: danmaku.update
actions.description: Update 1 to 100 bindings or current player tracks in input order. Each item sets enabled, offsetMs and/or displayFold absolutely; positive integer milliseconds advance, negative delay, zero resets. Any explicit offset in the supported range is accepted independently of analysis estimates. Persistent bindings (including bound trackId targets) require expectedRevision; each item is atomic and returns its own result or failure, without rolling back earlier items. Unbound tracks last for the current playback and have no binding revision. displayFold affects display grouping only; original caches remain unchanged.

actions.name: download_add
actions.title: add download
actions.description: Accept source or sources: magnet URIs, HTTP(S) torrent URLs or local .torrent paths. Optional downloadDirectory and createFolderForTask override defaults for these new tasks without changing settings. actions.name: download_directories

actions.name: download_import
actions.title: import download

actions.name: download_pause
actions.title: pause download
actions.description: Compatibility alias for download.set_paused with paused=true.

actions.name: download_preview
actions.title: Download preview

actions.name: download_read
actions.title: read download

actions.name: download_remove
actions.title: remove download
actions.description: Remove session entries for jobId or jobIds, keeping downloaded files. Returns per-item persisted jobs and failures.

actions.name: download_resume
actions.title: resume download
actions.description: Compatibility alias for download.set_paused with paused=false.

actions.name: download_select_files
actions.title: select_files download
actions.description: Replace the included file indices for jobId or jobIds without deleting data or changing paths. Empty selects none. actions.name: download_set_paused
actions.title: set_paused download
actions.description: Set paused for jobId or jobIds, including downloading and seeding. Returns persisted jobs and individual batch failures.

actions.name: followup_cancel
actions.title: 取消尚未执行的后续
actions.description: Cancel waiting, ready or failed delivery; does not interrupt an already started turn.

actions.name: followup_list
actions.title: 查询后续与等待条件
actions.description: List durable followups, actual thread/turn IDs, trigger facts and delivery errors. Also query the followups state view.

actions.name: followup_register
actions.title: 登记任务结束或事件发生后的 Agent 后续

Host unavailability remains visible in state.query followups.

actions.name: media_artwork_set

actions.description: Set independent persistent artwork overrides in one atomic batch. backdrop/poster/logo require entityId of a work; still requires an episode. Each entry supplies exactly one HTTP(S) url without userinfo or absolute local file, plus source:{label,url?}. Images are decoded and cached by X26 before commit; local files are copied. Source, actor and invocation are retained in metadata edits/activity. Overrides survive metadata refresh and need no provider identity or credentials. actions.name: media_identity_bind_batch
actions.title: media.identity.bind_batch
actions.description: Atomically accept explicit bindings in one batch. Local hierarchy is work -> release -> episode; files link to episodes. Two input modes must not be mixed within an entry. (1) Catalogue mode: every entry supplies workRef. kind=work binds/creates only the work; kind=release binds/creates the work and release; kind=episode binds/creates the work, release and exactly one episodeRef; kind=file also links an indexed file to one or more distinct episodeRefs. Without local IDs, the same provider refs reuse the same local hierarchy within this batch. For Dandanplay anime and Bangumi subject, omit releaseRef or repeat workRef: their episode catalogue is the release. TMDB TV requires releaseRef of objectType=season for all non-work entries. Work refs have scope=""; Dandanplay episode scope="anime/<animeId>", Bangumi episode scope="subject/<subjectId>"; TMDB season scope="tv/<tvId>/season/<number>" and episode scope adds "/episode/<number>". externalId is always the actual provider object ID, not the displayed episode number. Example (replace ANIME_ID and EPISODE_ID with verified provider IDs): {"requestId":"chosen-series-1","entries":[{"kind":"work","workRef":{"provider":"dandanplay","objectType":"anime","externalId":"ANIME_ID","scope":""},"reason":"User selected this work"},{"kind":"release","workRef":{"provider":"dandanplay","objectType":"anime","externalId":"ANIME_ID","scope":""},"reason":"This anime is its episode catalogue"},{"kind":"episode","workRef":{"provider":"dandanplay","objectType":"anime","externalId":"ANIME_ID","scope":""},"episodeRefs":[{"provider":"dandanplay","objectType":"episode","externalId":"EPISODE_ID","scope":"anime/ANIME_ID"}],"reason":"Verified episode identity"}]}. (2) Direct mode: ref + existing entityId + kind binds an external work/release/episode without fetching metadata, creating parents or cascading. Direct file bindings also require exactly one localEpisodeIds target where this ref is already accepted (including an earlier entry). New direct provider namespaces must be HTTPS origins; host canonicalizes them. Indexed remote files use source browse fileId as entityId and need no local byte probing. Preserves reason/evidence; host derives boundBy. requestId is durable and cannot be reused with different input.

releaseId.description: Catalogue episode/file: optional existing local parent release ID under workId. Omit to reuse/create from releaseRef (or workRef for anime/subject/movie).

localEpisodeIds.description: Catalogue: existing local episode IDs corresponding one-to-one with episodeRefs under the selected release. For kind=episode use entityId instead. Direct file: exactly one existing episode with this accepted ref.

actions.description: Save key/value or ordered changes using Classic setters. Each change has its own expectedRevision and reason. Batch results include revision, apply and individual failures; successful changes are not rolled back.

actions.name: state_describe
actions.title: Describe public state
actions.description: Describe registered public views, field schemas, units, namespaces, relations and query limits. Contracts are generated from the same registrations that project query results. No business writes or network requests.

actions.name: state_query
actions.title: Query public state
actions.description: Read registered public state with filters, projections, sorting, pagination and declared relations. No filesystem scan, source refresh, network requests or business writes. Secrets and authentication data are excluded. Default page size 50; use limit and select for output size. No default deadline or scan/concurrency ceiling. Results report pagination and per-source observations; unknown fields/views and invalid cursors return invalid_input.

filter.description: Field to operator/value objects. Predicates use AND. Scalar fields are filterable; arrays support contains with an exact member.

select.description: Top-level field projection. Omitted means all public fields.

orderBy.description: Scalar sort keys; default is source order. Equal keys retain source order.

include.description: Declared relation names mapped to query options (filter, select, orderBy, limit, include).

limit.description: Root page size. Defaults to 50. Relations have their own page sizes.

cursor.description: Opaque continuation for the same query over live data; it is not a transaction snapshot.

timeoutMs.description: Optional caller-selected execution budget in milliseconds. No deadline by default.

snapshotId.description: Null: observations do not form a global transaction snapshot.

sources.description: View name to UTC ISO-8601 read time; cached data can be older.

rows.description: Public projections described by each registered view. Relations contain rows, truncated and nextQuery.

nextCursor.description: Continuation for the same live query; null when no root continuation is known.

truncated.description: True when pagination or a resource limit omitted data.

warnings.description: Omissions: time_limit (only with explicit timeoutMs), relation_limit, sort_within_scan_window (only after an explicit timeout).

actions.name: subtitle_import
actions.title: 交入并保存字幕
actions.description: Copy local subtitle files into NipaPlay storage for indexed local fileIds, with declared BCP-47 language and source. Originals can be deleted afterwards; read-only video directories need no writes. Batch entries are saved individually; the reply gives every saved track. Supports ass/ssa/srt/vtt/sub/sup/idx (VobSub pair required). Saved tracks are restored next playback. Use subtitle.select for a persistent explicit default.

actions.name: subtitle_select
actions.title: 记录默认字幕

actions.name: subtitle_tracks
actions.title: 读取文件字幕事实
actions.description: Read persistent per-file embedded and external subtitle tracks, language, title, format, provenance, availability, probe status and default selection. Omit fileIds to read all indexed subtitle facts. No video probing.

actions.name: task_cancel
actions.title: Cancel task
actions.description: Request cancellation for jobId or jobIds and return accepted snapshots with individual batch failures. cancelling is not confirmation of stopping. Committed effects are still verified and recorded in receipt. Does not remove downloads or delete files.

actions.name: task_get
actions.title: Get task
actions.description: Read the complete task snapshot. succeeded means verification finished; receipt contains verified results. needs_decision contains optional executable option calls.

actions.name: task_list
actions.title: List task
actions.description: List persisted task snapshots, optionally filtering by state or type.

actions.name: task_wait
actions.title: Wait task
actions.description: Wait for a terminal state, a state/phase/decision change after afterRevision, or timeout. Progress alone does not wake the wait unless includeProgress is true. timeoutMs defaults to 60000 and is bounded to 0–60000. Without afterRevision, wait for the next meaningful change. afterRevision is the observed snapshot revision; a newer meaningful revision returns immediately. Returns the current job. Timeout does not cancel execution.

actions.name: ui_present
actions.title: 把卡片放到当前对话
actions.description: Append cards to your current NIPAPLAY_CHAT turn. kind=work uses workId; episode uses episodeId; task uses taskId (jobId); candidates uses items:[{workId,reason?}]; preparation uses title, optional workId and steps:[{label,detail?, exactly one entityId/taskId/followupId}]. actions.name: activity_report
actions.title: 记录有来源的发现
actions.description: Record a discovery with a source and arbitrary facts in activity. Does not wake the Agent. Source is supplied evidence; origin records the actual caller.

actions.name: agent_wake
actions.title: 唤醒 Agent 的主会话或指定会话
actions.description: Queue a new Agent turn with instruction and trigger facts. The host-configured agent device receives wakes from headless hooks and schedules; no conversation runs on the transfer device. Defaults to that Agent host’s main thread; optional threadId targets a conversation there. Busy turns are never interrupted. Uses the durable followup dispatcher.

actions.name: app_capabilities
actions.title: Read host capability facts
actions.description: Live host facts: app.instance identifies the process; app.capabilities reports supported features, provider/source readiness, credential references and required host setup, settings keys, action effects and remote policy. supported means an implementation exists; available means its declared host prerequisites are met, not a successful network probe. No secrets are accepted or returned. Remote writes follow local semantics; disk deletion/overwrite keep their existing NeedsDecision contract. On headless hosts indexing and download destinations treat media roots as read-only; file-channel operations use actual process permissions. Classic history/player/UI are absent. download.import indexes verified files without inferring identity; roots.remove unregisters the root without deleting indexed facts or disk files. settings exposes only returned keys.

actions.name: app_instance
actions.title: Identify the connected NipaPlay process

actions.name: danmaku_align
actions.title: danmaku.align
actions.description: Retired compatibility lookup for existing alignment requestId tasks. New requests return unavailable with migration to danmaku.analyze_alignment and danmaku.update.

actions.name: danmaku_align_apply
actions.title: danmaku.align_apply
actions.description: Legacy recovery only: execute an existing persisted alignment decision option with a task revision check. New analysis returns data and offsets are set through danmaku.update.

actions.name: danmaku_align_keep
actions.title: danmaku.align_keep
actions.description: Legacy recovery only: execute an existing persisted alignment decision option with a task revision check. New analysis returns data and offsets are set through danmaku.update.

actions.name: danmaku_analyze_alignment
actions.title: danmaku.analyze_alignment
actions.description: Estimate a fixed offset from up to 100 supplied source/media time anchors. Returns the upper median, absolute residuals in input order, span, evidence and confidence limits. Reads the binding revision; no task, Decision or persistence. Positive integer milliseconds advance danmaku (display time = source time - offsetMs).

actions.name: danmaku_attach
actions.title: danmaku.attach
actions.description: Bind a platform video to entityId, path or the current file (default). Existing platform/video tracks are reused; Classic dandanplay reuse records a binding, with jobId=null. Local pools prevent online acquisition. refresh=true fetches and replaces. Invalid required local ranges fail without mounting; outside-range errors are reported separately. Credentials are opaque host references.

actions.name: danmaku_attach_batch
actions.title: danmaku.attach batch
actions.description: Independent entries in input order using danmaku.attach. All schemas are validated before execution. atomic=false; each index returns its complete outcome (including binding/job IDs, decisions or failure). Successful entries are retained when another fails. Each requestId is scoped exactly as in the single action; credentials remain host references.

actions.name: danmaku_cache_delete
actions.title: danmaku.cache_delete
actions.description: Delete a specific source cache object and unload bindings using it. Binding evidence remains.

actions.name: danmaku_cache_prune
actions.title: danmaku.cache_prune
actions.description: Reclaim oldest recoverable danmaku pools to maxBytes (default 128 MiB). Imported unique copies are excluded. Defers while acquisition tasks are active; unloads evicted pools. Also collects unreferenced content files.

actions.name: danmaku_detach
actions.title: danmaku.detach
actions.description: Revoke this managed binding; unreferenced imported content files are deleted, provenance remains. Recoverable source cache remains subject to the cache budget. Classic local, automatic and Dandanplay tracks remain loaded with their managed binding detached. Other managed tracks are removed.

actions.name: danmaku_episodes
actions.title: danmaku.episodes
actions.description: Read a finite catalogue page. Zero duration means unknown duration. Acquisition requires a finite range within a known media duration.

actions.name: danmaku_export
actions.title: danmaku.export
actions.description: Export one committed binding as JSON to a new file in an authorized media folder. raw preserves original source fields; mapped applies its fixed offset without player filters. Readback is verified.

actions.name: danmaku_fetch
actions.title: danmaku.fetch
actions.description: Create a cancellable segmented acquisition/cache task for one explicit video/range. Does not modify player tracks. requestId makes retries idempotent. A failed acquisition receipt also reports available Classic cache, assigned/partial Next cache and currently loaded matching player tracks; existing comments do not prove this request succeeded.

actions.name: danmaku_fetch_batch
actions.title: danmaku.fetch batch
actions.description: Independent entries in input order using danmaku.fetch. All schemas are validated before execution. atomic=false; each index returns its complete outcome (including binding/job IDs, decisions or failure). Successful entries are retained when another fails. Each requestId is scoped exactly as in the single action; credentials remain host references.

actions.name: danmaku_import
actions.title: danmaku.import
actions.description: Import acquired danmaku using Classic local XML/JSON parsing and encoding support, including ARGB colors. Also accepts normalized JSON arrays (or {comments:[...]}): sourceTimeMs (nonnegative integer milliseconds), text, mode (positive integer), colorRgb (nonnegative integer, converted to RGB); optional platformId, sourceEntryId, originSource, sender, sentAt (strings), fontSize (positive integer). No registered source is required. Supply platform/platformVideoId; host records actor, origin and timestamp. Target entityId (file or episode), path, or current playback (default). Reimport replaces the same platform/video pool atomically, preserving track settings; empty or malformed files are rejected and leave the old track unchanged. Mounted immediately when the target is playing. File data stays in host storage; do not send large comment arrays through tool arguments.

actions.name: danmaku_import_batch
actions.title: danmaku.import batch
actions.description: Independent entries in input order using danmaku.import. All schemas are validated before execution. atomic=false; each index returns its complete outcome (including binding/job IDs, decisions or failure). Successful entries are retained when another fails. Each requestId is scoped exactly as in the single action; credentials remain host references.

actions.name: danmaku_offset
actions.title: danmaku.offset
actions.description: Compatibility alias for danmaku.update: set an absolute fixed offset in integer milliseconds, positive advances, zero resets. Does not refetch or accumulate offsets.

actions.name: danmaku_resolve
actions.title: danmaku.resolve
actions.description: Resolve a public URL or platform ID. Multiple parts return executable selection decisions. No persistence.

actions.name: danmaku_search
actions.title: danmaku.search
actions.description: Bounded transient title search. Unsupported sources report unavailable; no binding or task is created.

actions.name: danmaku_set_dedup
actions.title: danmaku.set_dedup
actions.description: Compatibility alias for danmaku.update: set absolute deduplicate with a binding revision check. deduplicate controls displayFold only; original source cache is preserved.

actions.name: danmaku_set_enabled
actions.title: danmaku.set_enabled
actions.description: Compatibility alias for danmaku.update: set absolute enabled with a binding revision check. deduplicate controls displayFold only; original source cache is preserved.

actions.name: danmaku_sources
actions.title: danmaku.sources
actions.description: List registered sources and capabilities. No network or persistence.

actions.name: danmaku_tracks
actions.title: danmaku.tracks
actions.description: List bindings and all current player tracks, including Classic and local pools with origin/platform/platformVideoId. loaded means mounted in the player registry, including Erika native danmaku; enabled is a track display switch. Neither reports whether comments are currently visible on screen. Accept entityId, path or current (default). Missing file locations are indexed without inferring work identity; no fetch or binding is created.

enabled.description: Track display switch; not proof of visible comments.

loaded.description: Mounted in the player track registry, including Erika native danmaku. Does not prove comments are visible at the current position.

actions.name: danmaku_update
actions.title: danmaku.update
actions.description: Update 1 to 100 bindings or current player tracks in input order. Each item sets enabled, offsetMs and/or displayFold absolutely; positive integer milliseconds advance, negative delay, zero resets. Any explicit offset in the supported range is accepted independently of analysis estimates. Persistent bindings (including bound trackId targets) require expectedRevision; each item is atomic and returns its own result or failure, without rolling back earlier items. Unbound tracks last for the current playback and have no binding revision. displayFold affects display grouping only; original caches remain unchanged.

actions.name: download_add

actions.name: download_directories

actions.name: download_import

actions.name: download_pause

actions.name: download_preview

actions.name: download_read
actions.title: read download

actions.name: download_remove
actions.title: remove download

actions.name: download_resume

actions.name: download_select_files

actions.name: followup_cancel

actions.name: followup_register

actions.name: media_identity_bind_batch
actions.title: media.identity.bind_batch
actions.description: Atomically accept explicit bindings in one batch. Local hierarchy is work -> release -> episode; files link to episodes. Two input modes must not be mixed within an entry. (1) Catalogue mode: every entry supplies workRef. kind=work binds/creates only the work; kind=release binds/creates the work and release; kind=episode binds/creates the work, release and exactly one episodeRef; kind=file also links an indexed file to one or more distinct episodeRefs. Without local IDs, the same provider refs reuse the same local hierarchy within this batch. For Dandanplay anime and Bangumi subject, omit releaseRef or repeat workRef: their episode catalogue is the release. TMDB TV requires releaseRef of objectType=season for all non-work entries. Work refs have scope=""; Dandanplay episode scope="anime/<animeId>", Bangumi episode scope="subject/<subjectId>"; TMDB season scope="tv/<tvId>/season/<number>" and episode scope adds "/episode/<number>". externalId is always the actual provider object ID, not the displayed episode number. Example (replace ANIME_ID and EPISODE_ID with verified provider IDs): {"requestId":"chosen-series-1","entries":[{"kind":"work","workRef":{"provider":"dandanplay","objectType":"anime","externalId":"ANIME_ID","scope":""},"reason":"User selected this work"},{"kind":"release","workRef":{"provider":"dandanplay","objectType":"anime","externalId":"ANIME_ID","scope":""},"reason":"This anime is its episode catalogue"},{"kind":"episode","workRef":{"provider":"dandanplay","objectType":"anime","externalId":"ANIME_ID","scope":""},"episodeRefs":[{"provider":"dandanplay","objectType":"episode","externalId":"EPISODE_ID","scope":"anime/ANIME_ID"}],"reason":"Verified episode identity"}]}. (2) Direct mode: ref + existing entityId + kind binds an external work/release/episode without fetching metadata, creating parents or cascading. Direct file bindings also require exactly one localEpisodeIds target where this ref is already accepted (including an earlier entry). New direct provider namespaces must be HTTPS origins; host canonicalizes them. Indexed remote files use source browse fileId as entityId and need no local byte probing. Preserves reason/evidence; host derives boundBy. requestId is durable and cannot be reused with different input.

actions.name: media_identity_bind_batch

actions.description: Atomically accept explicit bindings in one batch. Local hierarchy is work -> release -> episode; files link to episodes. Two input modes must not be mixed within an entry. (1) Catalogue mode: every entry supplies workRef. kind=work binds/creates only the work; kind=release binds/creates the work and release; kind=episode binds/creates the work, release and exactly one episodeRef; kind=file also links an indexed file to one or more distinct episodeRefs. Without local IDs, the same provider refs reuse the same local hierarchy within this batch. For Dandanplay anime and Bangumi subject, omit releaseRef or repeat workRef: their episode catalogue is the release. TMDB TV requires releaseRef of objectType=season for all non-work entries. Work refs have scope=""; Dandanplay episode scope="anime/<animeId>", Bangumi episode scope="subject/<subjectId>"; TMDB season scope="tv/<tvId>/season/<number>" and episode scope adds "/episode/<number>". externalId is always the actual provider object ID, not the displayed episode number. Example (replace ANIME_ID and EPISODE_ID with verified provider IDs): {"requestId":"chosen-series-1","entries":[{"kind":"work","workRef":{"provider":"dandanplay","objectType":"anime","externalId":"ANIME_ID","scope":""},"reason":"User selected this work"},{"kind":"release","workRef":{"provider":"dandanplay","objectType":"anime","externalId":"ANIME_ID","scope":""},"reason":"This anime is its episode catalogue"},{"kind":"episode","workRef":{"provider":"dandanplay","objectType":"anime","externalId":"ANIME_ID","scope":""},"episodeRefs":[{"provider":"dandanplay","objectType":"episode","externalId":"EPISODE_ID","scope":"anime/ANIME_ID"}],"reason":"Verified episode identity"}]}.
